chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the free man kills the slave, he is fined his value and disciplined. It was said: 'And if his value was twenty thousand dirhams?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The value of a slave does not exceed the blood money (diyah) of the free men.'

key_terms.الْحُرُّ: The free man (as opposed to a slave)
key_terms.غُرِّمَ: He was fined / liable for payment

ai.seo_question: What is the maximum compensation for killing a slave according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic ruling that while a free man killing another's slave incurs both financial compensation (gharamah) and corporal discipline (adab), the monetary value of the slave is capped at the standard blood money (diyah) of a free person. This principle, emphasized by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), prevents the slave's value from exceeding that of a free human, reflecting a balance between property rights and human dignity in Shia fiqh. It highlights the nuanced distinction between the slave's status as property and their inherent worth in compensation calculations.
